headline: RAB dissolved, replaced by SRB as new specialised police unit begins operations
summary: The Special Response Battalion (SRB) takes over RAB's assets and manpower, following years of human rights allegations and international sanctions.
details: The Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) has been officially dissolved and replaced by a new specialised police unit called the Special Response Battalion (SRB). The transition began yesterday following a gazette notification on the SRB law.

Under the SRB Act, all of RAB's powers, facilities, funds, manpower, assets, and liabilities have been transferred to the new force. The SRB will be composed of personnel from the police and other disciplined forces.
RAB was formed in 2004 and was credited with maintaining law and order, but it faced mounting criticism over allegations of extrajudicial killings and human rights violations.
In 2021, the United States imposed sanctions on RAB over these human rights abuses. The UN and various international rights organisations had also called for its dissolution.
The move comes after parliament passed a bill on September 10 to abolish RAB and the establishment of the SRB as a specialised unit under the police.
The director general of the SRB will be a police officer with a rank no lower than additional inspector general.
Opposition members in parliament criticized the move, arguing that changing the name while retaining the structure and facilities is merely a 'change of outer shell'.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, however, stated that RAB has been dissolved and the SRB has no connection with the former force.

headline_marked: [[Zafar Iqbal, Maksud Kamal among 8 charged]] at ICT for July uprising crimes
headline: Zafar Iqbal, Maksud Kamal among 8 charged at ICT for July uprising crimes
summary: The prosecution has filed formal charges against academic Dr Zafar Iqbal and former DU VC Prof Maksud Kamal over alleged crimes against humanity during the July uprising.
details: The prosecution has submitted formal charges to the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) against eight individuals, including writer Dr Muhammed Zafar Iqbal and former Dhaka University vice-chancellor Prof ASM Maksud Kamal.

The charges relate to alleged crimes against humanity during the July uprising, with the prosecution stating the accused were involved in incitement, conspiracy, and abetment of attacks on DU protesters.

The other accused include retired Appellate Division Justice AHM Shamsuddin Chowdhury Manik, DU Prof AKM Jamal Uddin, and Chhatra League leaders Saddam Hussain, Sheikh Wali Asif Enan, Mazharul Kabir Shayan, and Tanbir Hasan Shaikat.
Currently, Justice Manik, Prof Jamal Uddin, and Tanbir Hasan Shaikat are in custody, while the others remain absconding.
Saddam Hussain and Enan were previously sentenced to death in a separate case related to the July uprising just one day prior to these charges.
The prosecution specifically alleged that Prof Maksud Kamal made provocative statements and was part of a conspiracy that led to the attacks on protesters.
In a separate case regarding the 2013 Shapla Chattar crackdown, ICT-2 has appointed state defense counsels for 30 absconding accused, including former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
Additionally, ICT-2 summoned two Supreme Court lawyers to explain alleged contemptuous remarks regarding a verdict sentencing Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and six others to death.
